Alright, unpopular opinion time: audiobooks totally count as reading. I don't care what anyone says! Some people get really snobby about it, like you haven't truly experienced a book unless you've physically turned the pages. Come on. That's ridiculous. I listen to books during my commute, while I'm doing dishes, when I'm walking the dog. I'm getting through like three books a month now. Before audiobooks, I was lucky to finish one every couple of months. And the narrators? Some of them are incredible! There's this one guy who does all the voices differently and it's like watching a movie in your head. My friend keeps saying it's "not the same experience" and I'm like, okay, but I just finished a 600-page novel while you're still on chapter three of yours. Who's winning here? The whole point of books is the story, right? Doesn't matter how it gets into your brain. End of rant!
